correctness.rationale: Independence and domination force cyclic gaps 2 or 3. In a length-3 gap the two interior vertices have unique defenders; moving either adjacent defender toward the gap loses coverage on its other side unless the next gap on that side is short. In a length-2 gap either endpoint can defend the interior vertex exactly when its exterior gap is short. Thus neither consecutive 3s nor the pattern 3,2,3 are allowed, including the cyclic return to a lone 3. The forced 3,2,2 blocks and remaining 2s partition the gap word uniquely. For a+b blocks the count of distinguished-boundary tilings is n*binom(a+b,b); each undistinguished tiling contributes exactly a+b times even with periodic words. The small cases are correct: alternating pairs on C4, no secure pair on C5, all singletons on C3. In each unweighted census the logarithmic derivative has amplitude 1 at a simple smallest-modulus pole; equality in the triangle inequality forces phase 1 because the two allowed lengths are coprime. Thus the stated asymptotics have prefactor 1 and lambda<mu. An independent direct guard-replacement enumeration of every subset at n=4 through 20 matched the entire histogram, including P14=7z^6+2z^7 and P18=27z^8+2z^9; this is a finite cross-check only.
residual_risks: The defense swap is required only to preserve domination. Requiring post-swap independence is a different property.

value.rationale: The invariant is a complete size census of a natural defense property on a basic graph family. The local obstruction and unique block decomposition describe all configurations, not just minimum witnesses, and show that secure sets form an exponentially small fraction of independent dominating sets.
residual_risks: No claim for other graph classes, multiple attacks or swaps required to remain independent.
